newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan one-month NCD average yield at 6.286 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan one-month NCD average yield at 6.286 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank issued T$5 billion in one-month negotiable certificates of deposit on Monday at an average yield of 6.286 percent, a central bank official said.
The range of the bids was between 6.21 and 6.30 percent.
The issue coincides with a renewed bull run in Taiwan's stock market, where the index has pushed to a series of seven-year highs in recent weeks.
Monday was no exception, with the index notching another seven-year high close at 9,593.54.

Taiwan's overnight and short-term money rates soared into double digits in late June as investors diverted holdings into the red-hot share market, where daily turnover has spiked well above T$200 billion (US$7.2 billion) in many sessions.

Demand for cash for the stock market has been so high that some investors have liquidated their foreign exchange holdings into Taiwan dollars, fuelling volatility in trading of the recently depreciating currency.
The central bank has repeatedly issued NCDs to soak up liquidity during periods of peaking stock market turnover, first in March and April and again in June and July.
Dealers have interpreted the strategy as aiming to rein in the loose liquidity that many believe has fueled the rally.
The central bank maintains the issues are a response to the general liquidity sitution, not an explicit measure to to cool the stock market rally.
